keys.fb.h1: Tell us what broke. We will show you what changed.
keys.fb.lead: Rocktier apps have no analytics and no telemetry, so the only way we hear about a problem is when you tell us. This page explains where to write, what we put on the record, and how to check that a fix really shipped.
keys.fb.reach1: Inside any Rocktier app: open the Help menu and choose Send feedback. It opens a draft email on your device.
keys.fb.reach2: Or write to hello@rocktier.com, or use the contact page. A short description, the app version and what you expected to happen are enough.
keys.fb.reach3: Please do not attach private documents. A screenshot with the sensitive parts removed is usually more useful than the file itself.
keys.fb.publishTitle: What we publish, and what we do not
keys.fb.publish1: We have no user reviews that we are allowed to publish yet, so this page has no star ratings, no selected praise and no quotes. We will not invent any.
keys.fb.publish2: When someone lets us quote them, we will print the words unchanged, the unflattering ones too, next to the version that addressed them. Until then, the honest record is the changelog.
keys.fb.logTitle: A fix log you can check
keys.fb.logLead: These entries are copied from our public changelog, with real version numbers. None of them is presented as a response to a user email: they came from our own checks and from what we found while testing. Follow the link to read the full log.
keys.fb.log1: 2026-11-03, Rocktier Markdown 1.0.20: the preview's synced indicator could stay dark even when both panes were in sync. Fixed.
keys.fb.log2: 2026-10-24, Rocktier Markdown 1.0.17: Intel Mac builds added, so the app runs on older Macs as well as Apple Silicon.
keys.fb.log3: 2026-10-25, Rocktier OCR 0.2.11: an earlier update had removed the interface and the app opened to a blank window. The interface was put back.
keys.fb.log4: 2026-11-04, Rocktier Pic2WebP 1.9.20: in the default window the convert button could sit below the visible area. It now stays visible while only the settings scroll.
keys.fb.after1: We try to reproduce it on the same platform. If we cannot, we will write back and ask for one more detail.
keys.fb.after2: We fix the cause, not just the symptom, and add a check that would have caught it earlier.
keys.fb.after3: The change goes into the public changelog with its version number, so you can verify the claim instead of taking our word for it.
keys.fb.after4: We cannot promise every report lands in the next release. We can promise we will not quietly drop it, and that we will tell you if we decide not to do it.

keys.jr.f1.b: Every entry is sealed with AES-256-GCM, and the key is derived from your passphrase with PBKDF2. What sits on your disk is ciphertext, nothing more.
keys.jr.f2.t: One page a day, with mood

keys.openmd.lead: A .md file is just plain text, so any text editor can show you the raw characters. To see headings, tables, code blocks and images as a page, open it with a Markdown app. Here are the ways that work on both Windows and macOS.
keys.openmd.whatBody: Markdown uses plain punctuation for structure: a # for a heading, dashes for a list, backticks for code. The file stays readable forever, because it is text. A Markdown app renders those marks into a formatted page and, if you want, lets you edit the text beside it.
keys.openmd.mac1: Install the app once, then double-click any .md file in Finder. If another app is set as the default, right-click the file, choose Open With, and pick Rocktier Markdown.
keys.openmd.mac2: You can also drag the file onto the app icon in the Dock, or onto an open window.
keys.openmd.mac3: To make it stick, use Get Info, set Open With, then click Change All. macOS will remember it for that extension.
keys.openmd.win1: Install the app once, then double-click the file in File Explorer. If it opens in Notepad, right-click, choose Open with, then Choose another app and pick Rocktier Markdown.
keys.openmd.win2: Tick "Always use this app to open .md files" in that dialog to make it the default.
keys.openmd.win3: Dragging the file onto an open window works too, and skips the default-app setting entirely.
keys.openmd.extBody: Rocktier Markdown registers eight common Markdown extensions. They are all plain text, so even a file with an unusual extension can be opened from inside the app with File, then Open.
keys.openmd.fixTitle: When it does not look right
keys.openmd.fix1: You see the raw marks instead of a page: the file is open in a plain text editor. Change the default app as described above.
keys.openmd.fix2: Images are missing: Markdown stores image paths, not the images. Keep the pictures next to the .md file, or use paths that still resolve from where the file lives.
keys.openmd.fix3: Chinese text is garbled: the file was saved in a legacy encoding. Re-save it as UTF-8, which is what Markdown apps expect.
keys.openmd.offlineTitle: Do you need to upload it anywhere?
keys.openmd.offlineBody: No. Opening, reading and exporting a .md file all happen on your device. Rocktier Markdown has no account and no cloud, and the file itself never leaves the folder you chose.

keys.pd.f2.b: Turn a PDF into structured Markdown locally: headings, lists and paragraphs recovered on your machine.
keys.pd.f3.b: Black out sensitive text permanently, not just cover it with a shape that copy-paste can undo.
keys.pd.f4.b: Add page numbers and a visual stamp, or fill an existing form's fields without printing and scanning.
keys.pd.f5.b: Shrink image-heavy files to a shareable size while keeping the pages readable.
keys.pd.f6.b: Encrypt with a password, or strip it again when you need to.
keys.pd.f7.b: Sign PDFs with PKCS#7 certificates you manage yourself, and verify the signatures on anything you receive. The private key stays in secure system storage on your machine, and signing ships with the app: no second product, no extra fee.

Your SG receipt stays valid and unlocks the full app, so there is nothing to buy again. If your system blocks that copy, nothing is lost: the app keeps your certificates and asks you to re-import the key once.

keys.privacy.sub: One privacy policy for the whole Rocktier family. Every app works on your files locally, and no app connects to the internet unless you ask it to. No accounts, no uploads, no tracking.
keys.privacy.scopeP: This policy applies to every Rocktier app and to rocktier.com. The current family: Rocktier PDF, Rocktier Pic2WebP, Rocktier Markdown, Rocktier OCR, Rocktier CAD Viewer, Rocktier Write, Rocktier Journal and Rocktier Compressor. Each new app that joins is covered by this same policy.
keys.privacy.collectP1: Rocktier apps are built so they need no personal information to work. We ask for no name, no email, no phone number, no location, and no account. There is nothing to sign up for, and we run no usage analytics.
keys.privacy.collectP2: The files you compress, convert, edit, merge, or sign are processed on your device and never leave it. We have no servers that receive them and no way to see them.
keys.privacy.collectP3: Our apps contain no telemetry, no advertising SDKs, and no third-party analytics of any kind. If a version ever offers crash reporting, it is off by default: a report is sent only after you approve that specific report, and declining it costs you nothing.
keys.privacy.collectP4: A Rocktier app can make at most two kinds of requests, both described in full below: a license activation, and an update check that also re-checks your licence status. Both happen only when you ask for them: by entering a license code, or by clicking "Check for updates". Neither is needed to use the app, and it works fully offline without them. Some versions distributed through an app store ship without both entry points, because the store handles purchase and updates. A build that offers neither of them makes no network requests at all.
keys.privacy.listP: Across the family, these are the only three requests a direct-download build can make. They map to the two kinds described above: activation, and update checking (which may contact both our server and GitHub). Every one of them needs you to act first; none happens at startup or in the background, and none carries file contents, file names or paths.
keys.privacy.list1: when you enter a license code. Sends the code, a device fingerprint used for the activation limit, and the OS name.
keys.privacy.list2: when you click "Check for updates" while a receipt exists. Sends only the transaction id already in that receipt.
keys.privacy.list3: when you click "Check for updates". A public API call with no body, no query parameters and no custom fields; the repository name is part of the URL.
keys.privacy.listNote: Some app-store builds omit the menu entries that trigger these requests. What is left in a given build is visible in its Help menu, and the two kinds of request described above are the only ones any of them can make.
keys.privacy.updateP1: No Rocktier app checks for updates on its own. The app does not connect to the internet when it starts, while you work, or in the background. When you click "Check for updates", the app requests one small file that lists the latest version: and that is the only thing it asks for.
keys.privacy.updateP2: That request is a plain GET to GitHub's public releases API. The app sends no body, no query parameters and no custom fields: the repository name is part of the URL, and the only header the app sets is Accept. Standard request information: such as your IP address and the User-Agent supplied by your system, which may identify your operating system and CPU: is handled by GitHub under its own privacy policy, and we do not receive it. The request never carries your license code, your device identifier, or anything about your files. If a newer version exists, the app tells you and links to the official release page. We never download or install anything without asking, and we do not track which version you run.
keys.privacy.updateP3: Activating a license is a separate request to our own server. Its reply contains only a signed receipt, the product code and your device count: it does not return a version number, and the app never asks for one. On the latest releases, clicking "Check for updates" also re-checks your licence status with our server once: the request carries only the transaction id already in your receipt, and a refunded licence is deactivated locally. A build that ships without both entry points sends nothing to us.
keys.privacy.licenseP1: Activation is the only action that sends an identifier, and it happens only when you choose to activate a license or manage your devices. The app sends your license code, a device identifier, and the name of your operating system, so that we can count activations against the device limit and let you release a machine you no longer use.
keys.privacy.licenseP2: We store the license code, the device identifier, and the activation date. We store nothing else, and your documents are never involved.
keys.privacy.processP: All work happens locally on your device using its native capabilities, with no internet needed. Closing an app or deleting it removes its data from your device; nothing is kept anywhere else.
keys.privacy.shareP1: We do not sell, rent, trade, or share your data with anyone, for any reason.
keys.privacy.shareP2: When you download an app from a store (Microsoft Store, Apple App Store, or similar), the store operator handles standard transaction and device information under its own privacy policy. That handling is governed by the store operator, not by us, and we receive no personal data from it.
keys.privacy.secureP: Your data lives only on your device, protected by your operating system's own measures: app sandboxing, file permissions, and encryption at rest. There is no Rocktier cloud, no Rocktier database, and no data center that can be breached.
keys.privacy.kidsP: Rocktier apps are not directed at children under 13 and do not knowingly collect any data from anyone, including children. In practice, there is nothing of yours, or of a child's, for us to hold.
keys.privacy.rightsP: Under the GDPR (EU/UK), CCPA/CPRA (California), and China's PIPL, you have the right to access, correct, delete, and export your personal data. Because Rocktier collects no personal data, these rights are met by design. For any question, contact us and we will respond within 30 days.

keys.vs-online-tools.h2: Is offline processing safer than uploading?
keys.vs.safetyLead: Uploading is harmless for a public meme, and unacceptable for the documents most people actually need to compress or convert:
keys.vs.safety1Body: Client agreements and signed documents are confidential by definition; a compression tool has no business keeping a copy.
keys.vs.safety2Body: In many jurisdictions (HIPAA, GDPR) passing them through a third-party server can create compliance exposure you never agreed to.
keys.vs.safety3Body: "We delete files after one hour" is a policy, not a guarantee, and it is theirs to change.
keys.vs.safety4Body: Uploading gigabytes of personal photos to convert them to WebP wastes time and bandwidth you did not need to spend.
keys.vs.safetyVerdict: for anything private, offline wins: nothing is uploaded, so nothing can be retained, leaked, or read.
keys.vs-online-tools.h2.1: What do online PDF tools really cost?
keys.vs.costLead: Subscription pricing is how these tools make money: and the free tier exists to show you its own limits:
keys.vs.cost2Body: iLovePDF's free plan caps file sizes (merge 100 MB, compress 200 MB) and daily usage (compress: 2 files per day); Smallpdf limits free downloads per day across its tools.
keys.vs.cost3Body: metered and retried whenever the quota resets: the work stops until tomorrow.
keys.vs.costVerdict: Rocktier apps cost {p1}-{p2} once (Rocktier PDF is {p3}: about ten weeks of iLovePDF Premium), and never ask for another payment, an account, or a connection.
keys.vs.faq2q: Is local processing slower than a data center?
keys.vs.speedBody: A data center computes fast, but the bottleneck is not the computing: it is the round-trip. A 50 MB scan takes seconds to upload on a good connection and minutes on a bad one, then the result travels back. Processing the same file locally takes about a second and starts the moment you drop it.
keys.vs.speedVerdict: for typical files, local wins on speed: the upload never happens, and neither does the queue.
keys.vs.faq1q: Are desktop tools harder to install than a website?
keys.vs.faq1a: A Rocktier download is a single installer under 15 MB. You install it once and it stays out of your way: no account, no browser tab, no waiting for a server queue.
keys.vs.faq2a: For typical files, no. Uploading and downloading usually takes longer than the processing itself. Modern machines compress a PDF or convert a photo in about a second.
keys.vs.faq3q: Why pay once instead of using a free web tool?
keys.vs.faq3a: Free online tools monetize with ads, quotas, and your attention (and sometimes your data). Rocktier costs from {p1} once: no renewals, no caps, no ads.

keys.vs.faq4a: Yes. Updates are included in the one-time purchase. You are never asked to pay again.

feedback.fb.h1: Tell us what broke. We will show you what changed.
feedback.fb.lead: Rocktier apps have no analytics and no telemetry, so the only way we hear about a problem is when you tell us. This page explains where to write, what we put on the record, and how to check that a fix really shipped.
feedback.fb.reach1: Inside any Rocktier app: open the Help menu and choose Send feedback. It opens a draft email on your device.
feedback.fb.reach2: Or write to hello@rocktier.com, or use the contact page. A short description, the app version and what you expected to happen are enough.
feedback.fb.reach3: Please do not attach private documents. A screenshot with the sensitive parts removed is usually more useful than the file itself.
feedback.fb.publishTitle: What we publish, and what we do not
feedback.fb.publish1: We have no user reviews that we are allowed to publish yet, so this page has no star ratings, no selected praise and no quotes. We will not invent any.
feedback.fb.publish2: When someone lets us quote them, we will print the words unchanged, the unflattering ones too, next to the version that addressed them. Until then, the honest record is the changelog.
feedback.fb.logTitle: A fix log you can check
feedback.fb.logLead: These entries are copied from our public changelog, with real version numbers. None of them is presented as a response to a user email: they came from our own checks and from what we found while testing. Follow the link to read the full log.
feedback.fb.log1: 2026-11-03, Rocktier Markdown 1.0.20: the preview's synced indicator could stay dark even when both panes were in sync. Fixed.
feedback.fb.log2: 2026-10-24, Rocktier Markdown 1.0.17: Intel Mac builds added, so the app runs on older Macs as well as Apple Silicon.
feedback.fb.log3: 2026-10-25, Rocktier OCR 0.2.11: an earlier update had removed the interface and the app opened to a blank window. The interface was put back.
feedback.fb.log4: 2026-11-04, Rocktier Pic2WebP 1.9.20: in the default window the convert button could sit below the visible area. It now stays visible while only the settings scroll.
feedback.fb.after1: We try to reproduce it on the same platform. If we cannot, we will write back and ask for one more detail.
feedback.fb.after2: We fix the cause, not just the symptom, and add a check that would have caught it earlier.
feedback.fb.after3: The change goes into the public changelog with its version number, so you can verify the claim instead of taking our word for it.
feedback.fb.after4: We cannot promise every report lands in the next release. We can promise we will not quietly drop it, and that we will tell you if we decide not to do it.

open-md.openmd.lead: A .md file is just plain text, so any text editor can show you the raw characters. To see headings, tables, code blocks and images as a page, open it with a Markdown app. Here are the ways that work on both Windows and macOS.
open-md.openmd.whatBody: Markdown uses plain punctuation for structure: a # for a heading, dashes for a list, backticks for code. The file stays readable forever, because it is text. A Markdown app renders those marks into a formatted page and, if you want, lets you edit the text beside it.
open-md.openmd.mac1: Install the app once, then double-click any .md file in Finder. If another app is set as the default, right-click the file, choose Open With, and pick Rocktier Markdown.
open-md.openmd.mac2: You can also drag the file onto the app icon in the Dock, or onto an open window.
open-md.openmd.mac3: To make it stick, use Get Info, set Open With, then click Change All. macOS will remember it for that extension.
open-md.openmd.win1: Install the app once, then double-click the file in File Explorer. If it opens in Notepad, right-click, choose Open with, then Choose another app and pick Rocktier Markdown.
open-md.openmd.win2: Tick "Always use this app to open .md files" in that dialog to make it the default.
open-md.openmd.win3: Dragging the file onto an open window works too, and skips the default-app setting entirely.
open-md.openmd.extBody: Rocktier Markdown registers eight common Markdown extensions. They are all plain text, so even a file with an unusual extension can be opened from inside the app with File, then Open.
open-md.openmd.fixTitle: When it does not look right
open-md.openmd.fix1: You see the raw marks instead of a page: the file is open in a plain text editor. Change the default app as described above.
open-md.openmd.fix2: Images are missing: Markdown stores image paths, not the images. Keep the pictures next to the .md file, or use paths that still resolve from where the file lives.
open-md.openmd.fix3: Chinese text is garbled: the file was saved in a legacy encoding. Re-save it as UTF-8, which is what Markdown apps expect.
open-md.openmd.offlineTitle: Do you need to upload it anywhere?
open-md.openmd.offlineBody: No. Opening, reading and exporting a .md file all happen on your device. Rocktier Markdown has no account and no cloud, and the file itself never leaves the folder you chose.

privacy.privacy.title: Your files never leave your device.
privacy.privacy.sub: One privacy policy for the whole Rocktier family. Every app works on your files locally, and no app connects to the internet unless you ask it to. No accounts, no uploads, no tracking.
privacy.privacy.scopeP: This policy applies to every Rocktier app and to rocktier.com. The current family: Rocktier PDF, Rocktier Pic2WebP, Rocktier Markdown, Rocktier OCR, Rocktier CAD Viewer, Rocktier Write, Rocktier Journal and Rocktier Compressor. Each new app that joins is covered by this same policy.
privacy.privacy.collectP1: Rocktier apps are built so they need no personal information to work. We ask for no name, no email, no phone number, no location, and no account. There is nothing to sign up for, and we run no usage analytics.
privacy.privacy.collectP2: The files you compress, convert, edit, merge, or sign are processed on your device and never leave it. We have no servers that receive them and no way to see them.
privacy.privacy.collectP3: Our apps contain no telemetry, no advertising SDKs, and no third-party analytics of any kind. If a version ever offers crash reporting, it is off by default: a report is sent only after you approve that specific report, and declining it costs you nothing.
privacy.privacy.collectP4: A Rocktier app can make at most two kinds of requests, both described in full below: a license activation, and an update check that also re-checks your licence status. Both happen only when you ask for them: by entering a license code, or by clicking "Check for updates". Neither is needed to use the app, and it works fully offline without them. Some versions distributed through an app store ship without both entry points, because the store handles purchase and updates. A build that offers neither of them makes no network requests at all.
privacy.privacy.listP: Across the family, these are the only three requests a direct-download build can make. They map to the two kinds described above: activation, and update checking (which may contact both our server and GitHub). Every one of them needs you to act first; none happens at startup or in the background, and none carries file contents, file names or paths.
privacy.privacy.list1: when you enter a license code. Sends the code, a device fingerprint used for the activation limit, and the OS name.
privacy.privacy.list2: when you click "Check for updates" while a receipt exists. Sends only the transaction id already in that receipt.
privacy.privacy.list3: when you click "Check for updates". A public API call with no body, no query parameters and no custom fields; the repository name is part of the URL.
privacy.privacy.listNote: Some app-store builds omit the menu entries that trigger these requests. What is left in a given build is visible in its Help menu, and the two kinds of request described above are the only ones any of them can make.
privacy.privacy.updateP1: No Rocktier app checks for updates on its own. The app does not connect to the internet when it starts, while you work, or in the background. When you click "Check for updates", the app requests one small file that lists the latest version: and that is the only thing it asks for.
privacy.privacy.updateP2: That request is a plain GET to GitHub's public releases API. The app sends no body, no query parameters and no custom fields: the repository name is part of the URL, and the only header the app sets is Accept. Standard request information: such as your IP address and the User-Agent supplied by your system, which may identify your operating system and CPU: is handled by GitHub under its own privacy policy, and we do not receive it. The request never carries your license code, your device identifier, or anything about your files. If a newer version exists, the app tells you and links to the official release page. We never download or install anything without asking, and we do not track which version you run.
privacy.privacy.updateP3: Activating a license is a separate request to our own server. Its reply contains only a signed receipt, the product code and your device count: it does not return a version number, and the app never asks for one. On the latest releases, clicking "Check for updates" also re-checks your licence status with our server once: the request carries only the transaction id already in your receipt, and a refunded licence is deactivated locally. A build that ships without both entry points sends nothing to us.
privacy.privacy.licenseP1: Activation is the only action that sends an identifier, and it happens only when you choose to activate a license or manage your devices. The app sends your license code, a device identifier, and the name of your operating system, so that we can count activations against the device limit and let you release a machine you no longer use.
privacy.privacy.licenseP2: We store the license code, the device identifier, and the activation date. We store nothing else, and your documents are never involved.
privacy.privacy.processP: All work happens locally on your device using its native capabilities, with no internet needed. Closing an app or deleting it removes its data from your device; nothing is kept anywhere else.
privacy.privacy.shareP1: We do not sell, rent, trade, or share your data with anyone, for any reason.
privacy.privacy.shareP2: When you download an app from a store (Microsoft Store, Apple App Store, or similar), the store operator handles standard transaction and device information under its own privacy policy. That handling is governed by the store operator, not by us, and we receive no personal data from it.
privacy.privacy.secureP: Your data lives only on your device, protected by your operating system's own measures: app sandboxing, file permissions, and encryption at rest. There is no Rocktier cloud, no Rocktier database, and no data center that can be breached.
privacy.privacy.kidsP: Rocktier apps are not directed at children under 13 and do not knowingly collect any data from anyone, including children. In practice, there is nothing of yours, or of a child's, for us to hold.
privacy.privacy.rightsP: Under the GDPR (EU/UK), CCPA/CPRA (California), and China's PIPL, you have the right to access, correct, delete, and export your personal data. Because Rocktier collects no personal data, these rights are met by design. For any question, contact us and we will respond within 30 days.

vs-online-tools.vs-online-tools.h1: Your files deserve better than an upload form.
vs-online-tools.vs.lead: Every popular online PDF and image tool works the same way: your file leaves your device, travels to someone else's server, gets processed there, and travels back. Rocktier tools do the same job without your files ever leaving your machine.
vs-online-tools.vs.confOffline: Safe by design (contracts, records, client files)

vs-online-tools.vs-online-tools.h2: Is offline processing safer than uploading?
vs-online-tools.vs.safetyLead: Uploading is harmless for a public meme, and unacceptable for the documents most people actually need to compress or convert:
vs-online-tools.vs.safety1Body: Client agreements and signed documents are confidential by definition; a compression tool has no business keeping a copy.
vs-online-tools.vs.safety2Body: In many jurisdictions (HIPAA, GDPR) passing them through a third-party server can create compliance exposure you never agreed to.
vs-online-tools.vs.safety3Body: "We delete files after one hour" is a policy, not a guarantee, and it is theirs to change.
vs-online-tools.vs.safety4Body: Uploading gigabytes of personal photos to convert them to WebP wastes time and bandwidth you did not need to spend.
vs-online-tools.vs.safetyVerdict: for anything private, offline wins: nothing is uploaded, so nothing can be retained, leaked, or read.
vs-online-tools.vs-online-tools.h2.1: What do online PDF tools really cost?
vs-online-tools.vs.costLead: Subscription pricing is how these tools make money: and the free tier exists to show you its own limits:
vs-online-tools.vs.cost2Body: iLovePDF's free plan caps file sizes (merge 100 MB, compress 200 MB) and daily usage (compress: 2 files per day); Smallpdf limits free downloads per day across its tools.
vs-online-tools.vs.cost3Body: metered and retried whenever the quota resets: the work stops until tomorrow.
vs-online-tools.vs.costVerdict: Rocktier apps cost $4.99-$14.99 once (Rocktier PDF is $9.99: about ten weeks of iLovePDF Premium), and never ask for another payment, an account, or a connection.
vs-online-tools.vs-online-tools.h2.2: Is local processing slower than a data center?
vs-online-tools.vs.speedBody: A data center computes fast, but the bottleneck is not the computing: it is the round-trip. A 50 MB scan takes seconds to upload on a good connection and minutes on a bad one, then the result travels back. Processing the same file locally takes about a second and starts the moment you drop it.
vs-online-tools.vs.speedVerdict: for typical files, local wins on speed: the upload never happens, and neither does the queue.
vs-online-tools.vs.faq1q: Are desktop tools harder to install than a website?
vs-online-tools.vs.faq1a: A Rocktier download is a single installer under 15 MB. You install it once and it stays out of your way: no account, no browser tab, no waiting for a server queue.
vs-online-tools.vs.faq2q: Is local processing slower than a data center?
vs-online-tools.vs.faq2a: For typical files, no. Uploading and downloading usually takes longer than the processing itself. Modern machines compress a PDF or convert a photo in about a second.
vs-online-tools.vs.faq3q: Why pay once instead of using a free web tool?
vs-online-tools.vs.faq3a: Free online tools monetize with ads, quotas, and your attention (and sometimes your data). Rocktier costs from $4.99 once: no renewals, no caps, no ads.
vs-online-tools.vs.faq4q: Do the tools still get updates?
vs-online-tools.vs.faq4a: Yes. Updates are included in the one-time purchase. You are never asked to pay again.
vs-online-tools.vs.faq5q: Do web tools upload my files to their servers?
vs-online-tools.vs.faq5a: Yes, that is how browser tools work by design: the file is uploaded, processed on their servers, and sent back. Rocktier apps never upload; the file is processed on your machine.
